parsed.hypothesis_statement: Across synthetic daily price paths with matched unconditional return mean and variance, paths generated with volatility clustering will exhibit a larger reduction in terminal-wealth dispersion from inverse-realized-volatility position sizing relative to fixed-notional sizing than paths with independent identically distributed returns.
parsed.hypothesis_rationale: Volatility clustering causes recent realized volatility to contain information about near-term conditional variance, so inverse-volatility sizing can reduce exposure before or during persistent high-volatility episodes. Under independent returns with the same unconditional moments, realized volatility is less informative about future variance; therefore the relative dispersion-reduction effect should be smaller. This is distinct from threshold gating because it tests the role of conditional-variance dynamics in sizing efficacy.
